title: Problem Overview
content: **Erdős Problem #596** asks: for which pairs (G₁, G₂) does a Ramsey-type dichotomy hold? The dichotomy requires that finite n-colorings of G₁-free graphs always produce monochromatic G₂, yet countable colorings can avoid it. Erdős and Hajnal originally conjectured no such pairs exist, but (C₄, C₆) is a counterexample. The general characterization remains **OPEN**.
mathContext: The dichotomy combines a finite Ramsey property (unavoidable monochromatic subgraph under finite colorings) with a countable coloring property (avoidable under countable colorings). This tension between finite and countable is the heart of the problem.

title: Dichotomy Definitions
content:
**GraphProperty** is a predicate on SimpleGraph ℕ. **FiniteRamseyProperty**: for all n ≥ 1, there exists a G₁-free graph H such that every n-coloring of H's edges contains a monochromatic G₂. **CountableColoringProperty**: every G₁-free graph H admits a countable edge coloring with no monochromatic G₂. **HasDichotomy**: both properties hold simultaneously.

The coloring is typed as `(Σ v w : ℕ, H.Adj v w) → Fin n` for finite and `→ ℕ` for countable, encoding edge colorings as functions from the adjacency relation.
mathContext: The two properties are complementary: finite colors are insufficient to avoid monochromatic copies, but countably many suffice. This finite/countable gap is what makes the dichotomy remarkable. Formally: FiniteRamseyProperty $\equiv \forall n \geq 1, \exists H\;(G_1\text{-free}),\; \forall c : E(H) \to [n],\; \exists$ monochromatic $G_2$; CountableColoringProperty $\equiv \forall H\;(G_1\text{-free}),\; \exists c : E(H) \to \mathbb{N},\; \nexists$ monochromatic $G_2$.

title: The (C₄, C₆) Dichotomy Pair
content: **c4_c6_dichotomy** (proved from axioms): HasDichotomy IsC4Free ContainsC6. This combines **nesetril_rodl_c4_c6** (Nešetřil-Rödl: C₄-free graphs have the finite Ramsey property for C₆) and **erdos_hajnal_c4_trees** (Erdős-Hajnal: every C₄-free graph is a countable union of trees, enabling countable coloring). This disproves the original Erdős-Hajnal conjecture that no dichotomy pairs exist.
mathContext: Nešetřil-Rödl proved that for every n, there exists a C₄-free graph whose n-colorings all contain monochromatic C₆. Erdős-Hajnal showed C₄-free graphs decompose into countably many trees, giving a countable coloring avoiding C₆.

title: Main Problem (OPEN)
content: **ErdosProblem596**: asks for a complete characterization of all pairs (G₁, G₂) satisfying the dichotomy. **erdos_596** (axiom): asserts such a characterization exists. The problem cannot be resolved by finite computation — it requires understanding the structural properties that determine when the dichotomy holds.
mathContext: The problem asks not just for examples but for a complete classification. This is typical of Erdős problems: identify all objects satisfying a given property.

title: Related Problem: (K₄, K₃)
content: **erdos_595_k4_k3** (axiom): the pair (K₄, K₃) is conjectured to have the dichotomy (Problem #595). This asks: does every K₄-free graph admit a countable coloring avoiding monochromatic triangles, while for every n some K₄-free graph forces monochromatic triangles under n-coloring?
mathContext: Whether K₄-free graphs satisfy the dichotomy for triangles is a natural test case. The finite Ramsey property follows from Ramsey theory, but the countable coloring property is the open question.

title: Summary
content: **erdos_596_summary** (proved): packages the known results as a conjunction — (C₄, C₆) satisfies the dichotomy AND at least one dichotomy pair exists. **dichotomy_pairs_exist** (proved): constructs the witness from c4_c6_dichotomy. The general characterization of all dichotomy pairs remains **OPEN**.
mathContext: The summary replaces the earlier placeholder True theorem with a substantive conjunction of results. The existence proof ⟨IsC4Free, ContainsC6, c4_c6_dichotomy⟩ is the canonical witness.
